ai.description: The Asian Giant Tortoise reaches 60 cm in length. Its shell is dark brown to black with a flattened carapace and serrated posterior marginal scutes. It possesses prominent, enlarged scales on its forelimbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Asian Giant Tortoise is uniquely identified by its divided supracaudal scute, which is split into two distinct plates, unlike the single plate found in other Indian tortoises.
ai.habitat: The Asian Giant Tortoise inhabits humid evergreen and bamboo forests in hilly regions, typically ranging from lowlands up to approximately 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Asian Giant Tortoise is primarily crepuscular, often remaining inactive during the heat of the day and emerging at dawn or dusk to forage for fallen fruits and vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Manouria emys* is oviparous, laying 30–50 eggs in a unique mound nest. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season (typically May to October) in its Indian range.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Asian Giant Tortoise occurs in the evergreen forests of Northeast India, specifically in Assam, Mizoram, and Meghalaya, ranging from lowlands to 1,000 meters elevation.
